# POC: Omarchy-style tiling panels (branch `poc-omarchy`)

**Status: experiment, paused 2026-11-17.** Lives only on the `poc-omarchy` branch. Nothing here is adopted.
The rules in [README.md](README.md) and [omarchy.md](omarchy.md) still win. This page records what was tried,
what worked and what's open, so the work can be picked up later.

## The goal

The user (Nov 2026): *"a redesign that looks as close to Omarchy as possible."* The first step is the panels:
tile them the way a tiling window manager tiles windows, with the same animations.

Later steps (not started): bring more of the app's look and feel closer to Omarchy. Before designing one, look
at the real desktop: take screenshots with `grim` (the AI can do this itself), and read the live values with
`hyprctl getoption ...`. The user offered to record their screen if needed.

## Decisions the user made

| Question | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| How panels are arranged | **Dwindle**, Hyprland's default and the user's own `general.layout` | Chosen over keeping today's fixed places restyled, and over a master + stack layout |
| Gaps, borders, focus colour | **None**: no gap, no frame, no accent border on the focused panel | *"I like how my computer is set up (ie no borders)"*. The live desktop runs Omarchy's `window-no-gaps` toggle: gaps 0, border 0, rounding 0 |
| The line between panels | kept: the one 1px line the panels already had | not decided explicitly. Without it, panels with the same background run together |

## What the user sees

```
Alt+A only:          Alt+R (splits Chat):     Alt+J (splits Results):  Alt+V (splits Python):
┌──────────────┐     ┌──────┬───────┐         ┌──────┬───────┐         ┌──────┬───────┐
│              │     │      │       │         │      │Results│         │      │Results│
│    Chat      │     │ Chat │Results│         │ Chat ├───────┤         │ Chat ├───┬───┤
│              │     │      │       │         │      │Python │         │      │Py │Var│
└──────────────┘     └──────┴───────┘         └──────┴───────┘         └──────┴───┴───┘
```

- **Opening a panel** splits the panel the cursor is in (the last one focused or clicked): side by side
  when that panel is wider than tall, stacked when taller. The new panel goes right / below.
- **Closing a panel** gives its space to its sibling.
- **Full screen** (`Alt+Shift+<letter>`) grows the panel over the others; the same key puts the layout back.
- **Drag the line** between two panels to resize the split (10% to 90%). The arrangement is kept in
  `localStorage["delulu.tiles"]` and survives a reload.
- **Animations**, with Omarchy's values from `~/.local/share/omarchy/default/hypr/looknfeel.lua` (a
  Hyprland speed is in units of 100ms):

  | Hyprland | In the app |
  |---|---|
  | `windowsIn` 4.1, easeOutQuint, `popin 87%` + `fadeIn` 1.73 | a panel that opens scales up from 87% (410ms) and fades in (173ms) |
  | `windowsOut` 1.49, linear, `popin 87%` | a panel that closes shrinks to 87% and fades out (149ms), on top while its neighbours grow under it |
  | `windows` 3.79, easeOutQuint | the other panels slide and resize into place (379ms), content stretched during the move as Hyprland does |

## Interfaces

The server still decides **which** panels are shown, unchanged (`show_*`, `zoomed` in `state.py`). The new
`services/ui/assets/tiling.js` decides **where** they go and how they move. The two only meet through
data attributes.

```python
# ui/ui.py: every panel is a direct child of one container
rx.el.div(
    chat_pane(), tables_pane(), notebook(), variables_pane(), terminal_pane(),  # class "tile",
    rx.el.div(class_name="tile-splits"),        # drag handles; tiling.js fills it, React renders nothing
    class_name="tiles",
    custom_attrs={"data-zoomed": State.zoomed},  # the panel filling the window, "" for none
)
# each panel: custom_attrs={"data-pane": "chat", "data-shown": State.show_chat}
# (replaces the old class_name=rx.match(State.chat_layout, ("hidden", ...), ("alone", ...)))
```

```js
// assets/tiling.js
tree: Leaf{pane} | Split{a, b, ratio}               // dwindle tree, kept in localStorage
insert(tree, at: pane, pane) -> tree                 // the leaf `at` becomes Split{at, pane, 0.5}
remove(tree, pane) -> tree                           // the sibling takes the parent's place
layout(node, x, y, w, h, out) -> void                // rects per pane; side by side iff w > h
sync(animate: bool) -> void                          // see below
handles(zoomed) -> void                              // one .tile-split per Split, on its line
drag(pointerdown) -> void                            // sets node.ratio live, sync(false)
```

```js
// Alt+J pressed while in Chat, Chat and Results shown
keydown -> State.toggle_pane("python")         // server, unchanged
React sets data-shown="true" on the Python tile
MutationObserver(data-shown | data-zoomed) -> sync(true)
  before = on-screen rects (getBoundingClientRect, so it is correct mid-animation)
  tree = insert(tree, focused="chat", "python")  // dwindle: split the focused panel
  rects = layout(tree, container size)
  Python: place + pop in;  Chat: place + FLIP from its old rect;  closed tiles: pop out, then hidden
  after 430ms: dispatch window "resize"          // grids, editors, terminal re-measure
```

- Hidden tiles get `data-tile="gone"` (`display: none`) but stay mounted, so the "closing keeps it" rule
  still holds (cells, the shell and the variables are kept).
- `data-tile` is used instead of a class because React rewrites `className` on re-render.
- A window resize relayouts without animation, but only when the container's size really changed. Other
  code dispatches `resize` too, and that mustn't cancel a running animation.

## What worked (checked headless in Chromium via Playwright, 2026-11-17)

- The dwindle spiral (Chat, then Results, Python, Variables, Terminal) put each panel where expected.
- Full screen and back restore the same rects. Closing gives the space to the sibling.
- Dragging resizes the split, and the arrangement survives a reload.
- The pop-in and stretch animations play: a mid-flight frame shows the chat stretched while Results pops in.
- 238 UI tests pass. Lint is clean.

**Not seen yet on the user's real screen**, nor in the Omarchy web app window. Check that first when picking
this up.

## Open / known gaps

- **Spec conflicts, if adopted.** [README.md](README.md) says the Variables panel is a narrow column (now it
  gets half of what it splits) and describes fixed places (chat on top, a Terminal strip under the bottom
  row). Dwindle replaces both. Update the spec only when the user adopts this.
- **Dead code.** `chat_layout`, `pane_layout`, `variables_layout`, `terminal_layout` and `bottom_on` in
  `state.py`, and the `.bottom-split`, `.is-alone` and `--vars-width` CSS, are unused on this branch but not
  removed.
- **The cursor isn't always in the new panel.** Splitting follows the last panel focused or clicked. When a
  key opens a panel without moving the cursor into it, the next split still comes from the old panel. The
  spec says showing a panel by its key puts the cursor in it; check whether every panel actually does that.
- **The Terminal swallows `Alt` keys.** With the cursor in the shell, only the Terminal's own keys come
  back to the app (``Alt+` ``, ``Alt+Shift+` ``), so `Alt+R` there does nothing. That's existing behaviour,
  but it feels worse in a tiled layout.
- **No keyboard moves between panels**, eg `Alt+arrow` to focus a neighbour or `Alt+Shift+arrow` to swap two
  (Omarchy uses `SUPER+arrow` and `SUPER+SHIFT+arrow`). These are natural next steps; check
  `omarchy menu keybindings --print` for the letters.
- **No way to change a split's direction** (Hyprland's `togglesplit`), nor to reset the saved arrangement
  except `localStorage.removeItem("delulu.tiles")`.
- **The rest of the look** (title bar, bottom bar, fonts, colours read from the live Omarchy theme rather
  than hard-coded Everforest) isn't started.

## Picking it up

1. `git checkout poc-omarchy`, then `git merge main` (main will have moved on).
2. Read this page. Also check `local/omarchy-look/` on the machine it was made on: screenshots and
   `shoot.py`, the Playwright script that toggles panels and saves screenshots. It's git-ignored, so it's only
   there.
3. Ask the user how it felt on their screen, then pick from "Open / known gaps".
